title: verify: `dashboard-window.test.ts`'s NEGATIVE CONTROL cases read the real clock, so a run that crosses UTC midnight gets the probe's day-turn `not-run` and fails them (merge-queue red, run 38486827994)
body:
Filing gate **① a flaky test with a named landing point**, filed by the seat that hit it (AGENTS.md: whoever finds a flake fixes it or files it). Measured in the merge queue: run 38486827994, which went red. Filed by `domain:spec` seat 2 (#18549) · `os-justin` · session `session_01BRQ9Mp1yH7R1az6MaUM18H`. ⛔ Not a claim; grade and lane are triage's (`packages/verify` is `domain:cli`).

## What happened

- PR #23346's merge-group run 38486827994 ran from 23:52Z to 00:20Z, across UTC midnight. `Test Core (3/6)` failed in `@objectstack/verify`, `src/dashboard-window.test.ts`. The two failing cases are under "NEGATIVE CONTROL — an app plugin that keeps the window from storage (zero)", each with `AssertionError: expected 'the day turned after the run started …' to match /reads back logged_at = "2020-01-01T00…/` (extracted by the queue-triage comment `6158020656` on PR #23346).
- The same tree passed `Test Core` in the next queue group (run 38486917542, built on that group's commit). PR #23346 does not touch `packages/verify`.

## Why it is the clock, not the product

- The probe reads the real clock. When the day turns between the run's start and a measure's probe, it reports `not-run` with the reason "the day turned after the run started" (`packages/verify/src/dashboard-window.ts:800`). That is a deliberate, correct answer.
- The NEGATIVE CONTROL cases run on the real clock, and they expect the storage-rewrite reason (`reads back logged_at = "2020-01-01T00:00:00.000Z" …`). So a run that crosses 00:00Z gets the day-turn reason first and fails them.
- The file's own "THE DAY TURN" block already fakes `Date` (`vi.useFakeTimers({ toFake: ['Date'] })`) to pin that case on purpose. The controls do not, so they are midnight-sensitive.

## What done looks like

- The NEGATIVE CONTROL cases, and any other case in the family that reads the real clock and asserts a reason other than the day turn, freeze `Date` at a mid-day instant, as the day-turn block does, or another way that makes them independent of the wall clock.
- A pin that shows the controls pass with the clock set to 23:59:59.900Z.
- ⛔ The probe's own day-turn `not-run` stays as it is.

## Dedupe

MCP `search_issues` on objectstack-ai/objectstack, closed included: `verify dashboard-window test flaky UTC midnight day turned after the run started negative control`: 3 hits, #22208, #10717 and #8937, all closed. #8937 is the same class in another file (a fixture pinned to a calendar date red at UTC midnight); none is this file.
